summary: Bounded resumed verification of the final 261-file pinned subject completed with no new supported findings. All four initial mechanisms are corrected, including UTF-8 normalization before SQL persistence for malformed file display names. The final isolated fixture confirms durable metadata retains downloadable bytes after a simulated lost commit acknowledgement, disposition encoding is safe, and frameworkState performs no inline-body query. The recorded baseline timing evidence supports the scoped startup/API test isolation and wait adjustments. This is a pass for the assigned correction review, not a final full-suite or deployment result.

Fresh validity/membership/capability checks remain; token usage writes, session sliding-window writes and expired-session deletes are suppressed under the tenant advisory lock, removing the initial row/advisory lock cycle. The aging-token regression forces a stale timestamp during blob I/O and verifies download succeeds without touching it; the revoked-token regression still refuses bytes.

Reviewed frameworkState metadataList and its evidence count consumer. The regression includes frameworkState in the no-evidence_content-query assertion. Reviewed evidenceDisposition UTF-8 scalar replacement and fileInput normalization used by createFileEvidence and updateEvidence before persistence. The malformed filename regression checks PATCH success, exact bytes and an RFC 5987 replacement-character filename. Normalization changes display metadata and preserves artifact references, digest and approval scope.

limitations: Root owns final SQLite/PostgreSQL/browser/full check and Docker. This reviewer did not run heavy suites, a PostgreSQL concurrent deadlock injection, real PostgreSQL commit-loss fault injection, browser or live Docker/provider checks; final integration results remain separate from this correction-review pass.

The 33-pass evidence predates the final services/visua.ts filename normalization and the 14-pass startup evidence predates its final readiness/test wait adjustment. They cannot by themselves establish final-source integration success; the reviewed regressions remain applicable and root is rerunning full checks.

The commit-loss fixture simulates transport failure after a durable isolated SQLite commit. PostgreSQL JSONB compatibility is assessed from filename normalization before persistence and the existing API regression; a final PostgreSQL execution belongs to root.

Baseline timing numbers were collected by the separate diagnostic worker and are explicitly limited to today's registry, installed dependencies and ambient scanned checkout. Raw diagnostic stdout was provided through worker tool sessions; this review inspected the durable measurement record and corroborating source, not an independent controlled benchmark.

This resumed pass covers the four corrections, their regressions and bounded test-fixture/timing changes. It does not reopen unaffected original boundaries or assess later retention, provenance, supersession or auditor packaging work.
